title: Form 709 — the Ortiz family
instructions: Luis and Ana Ortiz, U.S. citizens, made the gifts below in 2025 and elect gift splitting. Compute taxable gifts and answer the compliance questions.

exhibits.title: Gifts by Luis
exhibits.content:
| Gift | Amount |
|---|---:|
| Cash to son | 60,000 |
| Stock to daughter (Luis's basis $40,000) | 30,000 |
| Tuition paid directly to granddaughter's university | 25,000 |
| Cash to Ana | 500,000 |
| Cash to their church | 100,000 |

rows.label: Taxable gift to the son reported by EACH spouse
Taxable gift to the daughter reported by each spouse
Taxable gift to the church reported by each spouse
Luis's total taxable gifts
rows.explanation: Son 11,000; tuition excluded; gift to Ana fully covered by the exclusion and marital deduction: **11,000**.

rows.label: Ana's total taxable gifts
rows.explanation: Her half of the son's gift (11,000); niece 5,000 and daughter 15,000 are under the exclusion: **11,000**.

rows.label: Daughter's loss if she sells the stock for $25,000
Who must file Form 709?
rows.explanation: Each has taxable gifts after splitting.

rows.label: Due date without extension
rows.explanation: Form 709 is due April 15 of the following year.

rows.label: Gift tax payable (assuming no prior gifts)
rows.explanation: The unified credit covers the taxable gifts.
